definitions.explanation: A large fortified building or group of buildings, historically used as residences for lords and for military defense.

examples.japanese: {大阪城|おおさかじょう}は{有名|ゆうめい}な{城|しろ}だ。
examples.english: Osaka Castle is a famous castle.

examples.japanese: {城|しろ}の{周|まわ}りには{堀|ほり}がある。
examples.english: There is a moat around the castle.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}には{今|いま}でも{多|おお}くの{城|しろ}が{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: Many castles still remain in Japan today.

notes:
{城|しろ} is the native Japanese reading, while {城|じょう} is used in compound names.

FAMOUS JAPANESE CASTLES:
- {姫路城|ひめじじょう} (Himeji Castle - UNESCO World Heritage)
- {大阪城|おおさかじょう} (Osaka Castle)
- {名古屋城|なごやじょう} (Nagoya Castle)
- {熊本城|くまもとじょう} (Kumamoto Castle)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {城|しろ}{跡|あと} (castle ruins)
- {城|しろ}{下町|かまち} (castle town)
- {城|しろ}を{築|きず}く (to build a castle)

KANJI READINGS:
- しろ: standalone noun
- じょう: in compound names (～{城|じょう})
